item: Gene synthesis cost per bp over a full 15-year window (2010 anchor, like-for-like with 2025)
queries_tried: 1) 'gene synthesis cost per base pair 2025 turnaround time days Twist Bioscience decline 15 years'; 2) 'gene synthesis cost per base pair 2010 2011 Carlson curves DNA synthesis price history dollars per base'; 3) direct WebFetch of Twist 2017 blog and 2025 Business Wire release
failure_reason: No single source publishes a like-for-like gene-synthesis price series spanning 2010-2025. The two 2010-11 figures found (about $1.30/base for simple genes and about $0.10/base for raw oligos) are quoted for different products than the 2025 gene-fragment price, so the ratio depends entirely on which anchor is chosen. The primary Carlson cost series was not directly retrievable; only secondary relays were reachable.
alt_sources_tried: 1) Twist Bioscience 2017 corporate blog (retrieved, gives $0.25-0.60/bp) [E-7031]; 2) Twist/Business Wire July 2025 price release (retrieved, $0.07/bp) [E-7030]; 3) NextBigFuture 2011 relay of Carlson data (retrieved, $0.10-1.30/base) [E-7065]; 4) Carlson-curve compilation page (retrieved, confirms post-2011 slowdown) - primary Nature Biotechnology 2009 Carlson paper not reachable
best_estimate: 18.6-fold total decline 2010/11 to 2025, about 18.7% per year, with a defensible band of 2.5-19% per year depending on the 2010-11 anchor. The like-for-like 2017-2025 vendor window is 14.8-23.8% per year and is the figure to rely on.
best_estimate_basis: Derived record E-7108 from inputs E-7065 (2010-11) and E-7030 (2025); the tighter 8-year figure is E-7102 from E-7031 and E-7030. Both endpoints are vendor list prices, so this is a list-price trend, not realised cost of goods.

item: Decomposition of DBTL cycle latency into queueing time versus processing time
queries_tried: 1) 'self-driving lab biology cycle time hours days closed loop autonomous experimentation review 2025 bottleneck queueing'; 2) "design-make-test-analyse" cycle time weeks medicinal chemistry pharma average number of compounds synthesized per project lead optimization'; 3) 'Ginkgo Bioworks foundry 2025 2026 restructuring capacity utilization datapoints automation Q2 2026 results'; 4) 'Arctoris Automata Insitro laboratory automation throughput experiments per week 2025 2026 status'
failure_reason: No published study decomposes measured DBTL wall-clock time into waiting versus running. Autonomous-lab papers report total elapsed time and experiments/day but not instrument idle/queue statistics. Pharma DMTA commentary reports target cycle times without a time-and-motion breakdown. Cloud-lab post-mortems name scheduling as a failure mode qualitatively.
alt_sources_tried: 1) Royal Society Open Science 2025 SDL review [E-7056] - characterises operation horizons, no queue decomposition; 2) cloud-lab practitioner post-mortem [E-7041] - names unpredictable scheduling and human sample handling as core failure modes, no numbers; 3) Ginkgo Q2 2026 earnings call [E-7037] - reports a fourfold increase in available lab hours from moving to 168 h/week, which is a queue-capacity statement; 4) A-Lab and mobile-chemist papers [E-7042, E-7044] - report experiments/day only
best_estimate: Queueing dominates: roughly 60-85% of elapsed DBTL time in a production setting is waiting (instrument availability, batching to fill a plate or a synthesis order, human handoffs, shipping for outsourced steps), with 15-40% actual processing.
best_estimate_basis: Inference from two convergent proxies. (a) Ginkgo's own claim that moving to 24/7 operation quadrupled usable lab hours [E-7037] implies the prior regime was idle roughly 75% of the time, i.e. availability rather than instrument speed was binding. (b) A make-on-demand compound order takes 3-4 weeks of calendar time [E-7032] while the underlying parallel-synthesis chemistry is hours to days, implying most of that interval is batching and queueing. Cross-check: an aspirational 5-day DMTA cycle [E-7045] against real cycles reported in weeks [E-7045] leaves the difference as non-processing time. This is a reasoned estimate, not a measurement, and is labelled as such wherever used.

item: Cost per experiment, in a comparable unit, for cloud labs and automated foundries
queries_tried: 1) 'Emerald Cloud Lab shutdown closure 2025 2026 status'; 2) 'Strateos shut down cloud lab 2023 2024 assets acquired status'; 3) 'Ginkgo Bioworks foundry 2025 2026 restructuring capacity utilization datapoints automation Q2 2026 results'; 4) 'Arctoris Automata Insitro laboratory automation throughput experiments per week 2025 2026 status'; 5) WebFetch of the cloud-lab sector post-mortem
failure_reason: No operator publishes a price per experiment in a unit comparable across platforms. Pricing is quoted per protocol, per instrument-hour or per bespoke program, and is not public for any of Emerald Cloud Lab, Strateos/Multiply Labs, Ginkgo, Arctoris, Insitro or Recursion. Ginkgo's SEC filings report revenue and Adjusted EBITDA but do not disclose an experiment count that would allow a revenue-per-experiment derivation.
alt_sources_tried: 1) Ginkgo 8-K exhibit 99.1 Q2 2026 [E-7036] - revenue and loss disclosed, no experiment denominator; 2) Emerald Cloud Lab public site and PitchBook profile [E-7039] - no pricing; 3) Strateos/Multiply Labs and Tracxn profiles [E-7038] - no pricing; 4) cloud-lab practitioner post-mortem [E-7041] - gives capital cost per pipeline, about $5M, not cost per experiment; 5) Arctoris and Automata vendor pages [E-7059, E-7064] - relative multiples only
best_estimate: Order of magnitude $10-100 per fully automated well-scale experiment in a shared facility, and $1,000-10,000 per bespoke multi-step protocol run. Amortised capital alone is roughly $5-15 per experiment.
best_estimate_basis: Derived from [E-7041]: about $5M capital per automated pipeline, amortised over 5 years at 1e5-5e5 experiments/year gives $2-10 per experiment in capital alone; adding consumables, reagents, facility and staff typically multiplies capital-only figures by 3-10x in laboratory cost accounting, yielding the $10-100 band. Cross-check on the upper tier: Insilico reports about $2.6M for a full preclinical program to development candidate [E-7058], which at a few thousand discrete experiments implies high-hundreds to low-thousands of dollars per experiment for complex protocols. This is an estimate with roughly one order of magnitude of uncertainty and is not used to support any conclusion in the report.

item: Absolute experiments-per-week throughput for Automata, Arctoris, Insitro and Emerald Cloud Lab
queries_tried: 1) 'Arctoris Automata Insitro laboratory automation throughput experiments per week 2025 2026 status'; 2) 'Automata LINQ lab automation company 2026 throughput samples per day customers status funding'; 3) "Emerald Cloud Lab" 2026 news winding down layoffs Carnegie Mellon cloud lab operations'; 4) WebFetch of the Emerald Cloud Lab Wikipedia entry
failure_reason: Operating status was successfully verified for all four, but none publishes an absolute throughput figure. Automata publishes a relative multiple (5x) against an unspecified baseline; Arctoris publishes a relative multiple (10x) with an undisclosed base; Insitro publishes no platform throughput figure; the most recent Emerald Cloud Lab figure located is an instrument count from July 2020, not a throughput rate.
alt_sources_tried: 1) Automata product page plus Molecular Devices partnership release [E-7064]; 2) Arctoris Biophysics Centre of Excellence announcement via SelectScience [E-7059]; 3) insitro CombinAbleAI/TherML announcement [E-7060]; 4) Emerald Cloud Lab Wikipedia and PitchBook/ZoomInfo profiles [E-7039, E-7040]
best_estimate: 1e3-1e5 discrete assay operations per week per facility for the integrator-class platforms (Automata, Arctoris, ECL), which is 1-3 orders of magnitude below the company-reported 2.2e6 imaged wells per week at Recursion [E-7035] because the latter counts imaged wells rather than distinct assay operations.
best_estimate_basis: Bounded from below by the peer-reviewed parallel protein pipeline figure of hundreds of purified proteins per week per operator [E-7048] and by 96 constructs per week per pipeline [E-7049], scaled by the tens of instruments these facilities operate [E-7040]; bounded from above by the observation that no integrator-class facility reports the imaged-well volumes of a dedicated phenomics platform [E-7035]. The band is wide and no conclusion in the report depends on it.

item: Direct measurement of the correlation r between any specific in vitro assay readout and clinical utility
queries_tried: 1) 'predictive validity drug discovery screening cascade Scannell Bosley 2016 PLOS ONE model correlation more important than throughput'; 2) 'Scannell 2022 Nature Reviews Drug Discovery predictive validity what it is why it matters key argument bottleneck screening models'; 3) 'organ-on-chip microphysiological system throughput compounds per week versus in vivo animal study duration weeks predictive validity translational'
failure_reason: The predictive-validity literature defines the quantity and models its consequences but reports no empirically estimated r for a named assay. Scannell and colleagues state explicitly that predictive validity is under-managed precisely because it cannot be measured until outcomes are known [E-7063], which is a structural obstacle rather than a gap in my search.
alt_sources_tried: 1) Scannell and Bosley PLOS ONE 2016 [E-7061, E-7062] - simulation with assumed r values, not measured; 2) Scannell et al. NRDD 2022 [E-7063] - review, states the measurement problem; 3) Ingber NRG 2022 on organs-on-chips [E-7055] - throughput and qualitative predictivity, no r; 4) Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology [E-7018, E-7020] - measures replication, which is precision, not clinical predictivity
best_estimate: For a typical target-based biochemical screen r is plausibly in the range 0.1-0.3 against clinical utility, and for the best-validated phenotypic or patient-derived models perhaps 0.4-0.6. The absolute values are unmeasured.
best_estimate_basis: Inference anchored to observed outcomes rather than to any published r. Phase I to approval cumulative success in the 7-14% band named in the common brief's anchors, combined with the Scannell cascade arithmetic in which a four-step cascade at r = 0.3 needs about 739 candidates per true positive versus 14 at r = 0.9 [E-7062], is consistent with an effective end-to-end r in the low tenths. Independently, the 16% intention-to-treat positive predictive value of published preclinical findings [E-7020] caps how high the correlation of the upstream models can be. Every use of r in the report is either a source-supplied simulation parameter or an explicitly flagged [INFER]; no conclusion rests on a measured value that does not exist.
